# PR #2065 ARM native diagnostic protocol — reviewed source pair

This folder contains a functional replacement GitHub Actions diagnostic protocol. The exact source pair and full semantic reports remain reviewed and frozen. This replacement overlay has not been committed, published or dispatched, and no ARM release build or sample has run. A workflow dispatch still requires an externally reviewed exact diagnostic commit SHA; every stage checks the live source pair and its pinned CI and Codecov results. The prior v1 through v6 proposals and their hashes remain preserved separately.

The first reviewed overlay (`f8322f2505aef9fe09f0485b50e30c37ad12518e`) was dispatched as run `38793802732` and failed before any build or sample: checkout depth five omitted the pinned baseline, which is seven commits behind the overlay. Its failure record and zero-row outcome remain retained. This replacement protocol checks out full history in all four runtime job paths and keeps every exact ancestry and source guard. It has not been dispatched.

The exact baseline is PR #2022 head `edb31fdf0307bbadf5ef141dec2dfcabf027312d`; the proposed candidate is draft PR #2065 head `d3729e21d9647a64f6c05442c56acb8880485abe`, a descendant of the baseline. The diagnostic overlay must be one addition-only commit directly atop the candidate. Its own commit SHA cannot be embedded in its tracked pair.json. A required workflow-dispatch input therefore supplies the independently reviewed exact diagnostic commit SHA, checked against the executing GITHUB_SHA, sole candidate parent, addition-only changed-file set, and an in-commit file-hash manifest. The preflight and each runtime stage check actual remote PR heads, draft state, exact successful CI run 38788622449 and four pinned Codecov check-run IDs by name/head/conclusion in one snapshot per stage; there is no polling. The source-only Git inventory digests are pinned for all 4,877 baseline and 4,895 candidate Rust/Cargo files. Complete semantic hashes came from fresh local Rust 1.99.1/default-feature dev builds, with independent raw-output verification and source-bound classification of every graph delta. ARM release binaries must reproduce those hashes before any sample. The first 354e semantic collection exposed an imported NonNullable order regression and remains retained as historical adverse evidence; d372 is the corrected source pair. The final numeric summary checks currentness again and marks drift or unavailable checks ineligible while retaining any rows.

A push of the reviewed diagnostic branch runs only a small registration job: no checkout, build, or sample. GitHub requires this first run before an API/CLI workflow_dispatch against a branch whose workflow is absent from default ([workflow_dispatch event docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_dispatch)). The exact reviewed commit SHA is then supplied as the required dispatch input. Every build and measurement job is gated to that dispatch event. The event-driven DAG builds baseline and candidate production binaries concurrently on separate `ubuntu-24.04-arm` jobs. Two separate jobs compile the default and instrumented layout observations. Every build uses Rust 1.99.1, default features, opt-level 3, full LTO, one codegen unit, and an isolated owned Cargo target, with at least 8 GiB per job and jobs=2. Full Git source inventories, Cargo JSON compiler artifacts with `fresh=false`, release flags, binary hashes, and ELF identity are checked. The private producer rejects all unapproved files and directories before upload. The six allowlisted payloads per arm are CLI, timing probe, graph probe, N-API addon, Cargo JSON, and source inventory, plus their digest manifest; the private same-run transfer expires after one day. Public artifacts exclude binaries, sources, raw reports, and profiles.

One measurement VM downloads and verifies both arms. Untimed semantic preflight compares complete sorted structured graph sites/nodes/edges/importer views for 18 physical fixture configurations, including the inherited 41-file receiver-order fixture, the seven-file imported-utility-order fixture, and no-call controls. It compares complete CLI JSON outputs, exits, warnings, and signatures separately for both source versions. All per-arm hashes must be independently reviewed and pinned; baseline reports may legitimately lack new candidate typed/nullish receipts. The compiled N-API adapter checks the original **17 effects entry requests plus one check** and a separate **four imported-utility requests plus one check** per arm, CJS and ESM Promise return and deep equality, and full CLI parity. The imported-utility adapter uses the exact collected physical order: early, late, late-shapes, shadows; a key-set guard rejects extra or missing entries. Only the candidate is checked against the original 25 effects and new four imported-utility effects with exact lines in its committed test; the baseline receives separately pinned full reports.

The 31 consuming workloads comprise 16 inherited #2022 controls and 15 typed/nullish/cycle cases; the imported-utility fixture is untimed. The sampling controller retains startup, calibration, pilot, and every CPU/user/system/wall/RSS long row, with eight fixed balanced blocks and at most 992 long rows. Missing rows, noisy pilot, or higher cost are reported without favorable retry. Build/layout/preflight failures still enter an always-run numeric curation path that records each upstream status and remote drift separately, then marks the gate ineligible; sampling requires both frozen binary artifacts and successful semantic/N-API preflight. Startup and calibration rows are written after each arm, so a second-arm failure retains the first row. Timed resource values survive output-inspection failure with an explicit invalid signature. The proposed 180-minute sampling budget is a bound to review, not evidence of feasibility or performance.

This protocol has local static/unit validation and untimed full semantic outputs from separate local dev builds. No ARM build, benchmark, diagnostic-branch push, or dispatch has run. The exact overlay commit and externally supplied SHA must match its reviewed bytes before branch registration and dispatch. PR #2065 remains draft until real native performance and all repository gates pass.
